summary: F5 and F6 are fixed. Gateway traffic that carries no viewer identity is the owner's own traffic and now maps to owner, while a named gateway viewer with an unknown or missing role gets public. A standalone server with no host token now serves its owner and accepts sync pushes. Temp tests cover both fixes, every changed line is now covered, and I accept the BrowserService exemption. The durable Electron E2E test still fails because of a real defect in the edited test: it calls `app.server` after `app.quit()`.

findings.body: After `await app.quit()`, the test calls `app.server.rpc.browser.open(...)`. `ElectronTestApp.server` reads `this.running`, which throws 'Halo is closed. Call app.open() before using it.' (`ElectronTestApp.ts:211`). The durable run fails at this line, so the test no longer checks that the extension keeps running after Electron quits. Take the `server` fixture from `e2eTest` (`e2eTest.ts:82-120`), which runs independently of Electron, and call `server.rpc.browser.open({ url: extension.url })` and `server.rpc.browser.snapshot(...)` after the quit. Close the browser session too.
